target.title: fix(sessions): auto-generate session titles via AI summarization
target.body:
Closes #77165
Related #89705

## Summary

- **Fix classification:** Root-cause feature completion for opt-in model-generated session titles.
- **Maintainer-ready confidence:** High for the scoped local update. The submitted diff has focused validation and final review; remote CI and maintainer product/privacy acceptance remain pending after submit.
- **Root cause:** Saved sessions had no durable generated-title source of truth, so session lists fell back to manual names, first user message snippets, or session ids.
- **Why this is root-cause fix:** This fixes the source-of-truth state lifecycle because `autoTitle` is created once in the reply lifecycle, stored on the session entry, cleared with session reset/rollover state, and projected to gateway/Control UI instead of being recomputed by display fallbacks.
- **Patch quality notes:** The broad catches are intentional isolation for a non-blocking background title task; failures log or no-op instead of interrupting the user reply. The `null`/`false` returns are explicit skip/no-title states for invalid, absent, stale, or manually titled sessions.
- **Why it matters / User impact:** Users with many saved sessions can identify conversations by concise generated titles instead of first-message or id fallbacks once the feature is enabled.
- **What did NOT change:** Not changed / out of scope: no unrelated behavior, no default enablement, no migration/backfill, no manual rename UI, no channel/provider/plugin capability change, no agent-facing `sessions_list` behavior change, and no ConfigIO or generic session-store policy change.
- **Architecture / source-of-truth check:** `autoTitle` is persisted as session metadata and projected outward; gateway and UI do not maintain a second title source. Runtime auth selection for this path is kept behind an internal helper so the public runtime-auth helper contract is not expanded.
- **Related open PR / same-contract scan:** Related context is tracked in #89705. This update is scoped to the existing PR branch for #77165 and does not open a competing new PR or broaden the public provider-auth helper contract.
- **Out of scope:** Manual rename UI, migration/backfill for existing sessions, default-enabling generated titles, provider/channel/plugin capability changes, agent-facing `sessions_list` behavior, ConfigIO typing, generic session-store merge policy, and test-project routing.
- **Target test file:** `src/auto-reply/reply/session-title-generator.test.ts`, `src/gateway/session-utils.test.ts`, `src/gateway/server.sessions.list-changed.test.ts`, and focused Control UI session tests.
- **Scenario locked in:** Enabled sessions with enough direct user turns get one bounded stored title; manual titles and stale async writes prevent overwrite; reset/new/rollover clears generated titles while preserving manual display names.
- **Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail:** The feature spans title creation, persistence, reset/rollover cleanup, gateway projection, and UI projection; the final diff removes earlier nonessential `sessions_list`, ConfigIO, generic store merge, test-routing, and public helper expansion work.
- **Risk labels considered:** compatibility, session-state, public config/schema, auth-provider routing, availability, privacy/cost boundary.
- **Risk explanation:** The highest-risk area is sending bounded transcript excerpts to the title model when the feature is enabled.
- **Why acceptable:** The feature is opt-in/default-off, filters non-direct and non-text user records, caps input size, skips manual-title sessions, guards stale writes by `sessionId`, and runs after reply delivery.

## What Problem This Solves

What problem does this PR solve?
Users with many saved sessions only had manual names, first-message fallbacks, or session-id fallbacks, so session history was hard to scan and search. This PR adds an opt-in model-generated title path that stores a durable `autoTitle` once enough direct user turns exist.

Why does this matter now?
The linked feature asks for concise session titles after a configurable number of turns, with manual names taking precedence and without blocking normal replies.

What is the intended outcome?
When `sessionTitle.enabled` is true, OpenClaw can create one concise title for a session in the background, persist it as `autoTitle`, show/search it in gateway and Control UI session lists, and clear it on reset/new/rollover without removing manual names.

What is intentionally out of scope?
Manual rename UI, migration/backfill for existing sessions, default-enabling generated titles, provider/channel/plugin capability changes, agent-facing `sessions_list` behavior, ConfigIO typing, generic session-store merge policy, and test-project routing.

What does success look like?
Default-off behavior is unchanged; enabled sessions get bounded background title writes; manual labels/display names/origin labels/subjects remain higher priority; stale async writes are skipped; gateway/UI consumers read the same stored title field.

What should reviewers focus on?
Please focus on the session-title lifecycle: config opt-in, transcript filtering, session model/auth selection, stale-write guard, reset/rollover cleanup, and gateway/UI propagation of `autoTitle`.

## Linked context

Which issue does this close?
Closes #77165

Which issues, PRs, or discussions are related?
Related #89705

Was this requested by a maintainer or owner?
This continues the existing PR for the linked feature request; product/privacy tradeoffs remain maintainer-owned.

Implementation notes:
- The title worker reads only direct user text from the transcript head, skips heartbeat and inter-session/tool-mediated provenance, ignores textless/media-only records, caps each message and the total model input, and writes only if the persisted `sessionId` still matches.
- It skips sessions that already have a manual title source.
- Background title generation uses the active session model/auth context.
- This update does not add a public runtime-auth helper API expansion; the Plugin SDK API hash is regenerated for the public config/session type surface affected by this feature.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** Model-generated session title creation, persistence, stale async write prevention, reset/rollover cleanup, manual-title precedence, gateway list/search/event propagation, Control UI display/filter/event patching, config docs/baseline, and public API baseline consistency.
- **Real environment tested:** Local OpenClaw task worktree on Linux with focused Vitest suites and repository baseline/surface checks. A full live Control UI screenshot/video was not captured for this scope-shrink pass; the current update is covered by focused gateway/UI/session tests and remote CI will rerun after submit.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:** See the validation list below. The commands were run through the daily-fix validation wrapper in the task worktree.
- **Evidence after fix:** All listed validations passed and the verification marker binds the current committed shrink diff to those evidence files.
- **Observed result after fix:** The PR diff is now one commit and 34 files, with nonessential `sessions_list`, ConfigIO, generic store merge policy, test-project routing, and Plugin SDK runtime-auth helper expansion removed.
- **What was not tested:** Full repository validation and full `check:changed` were not rerun. Full live browser/Control UI proof was not captured. Remote CI is expected to run after submit.
- **Proof limitations or environment constraints:** Local proof is focused rather than full live UI/browser proof for this scope-shrink pass. The feature remains opt-in/default-off and bounded to reduce privacy and availability risk.

## Tests and validation

Which commands did you run?

- `pnpm exec vitest --config test/vitest/vitest.auto-reply.config.ts src/auto-reply/reply/session-title-generator.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/conversation-label-generator.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/get-reply-run.media-only.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/session.test.ts --run` — passed 4 test files / 233 tests.
- `pnpm exec vitest --config test/vitest/vitest.gateway.config.ts src/gateway/session-utils.test.ts src/gateway/server.sessions.list-changed.test.ts --run` — passed 4 test files / 366 tests.
- `pnpm exec vitest --config test/vitest/vitest.ui.config.ts ui/src/ui/controllers/sessions.test.ts ui/src/ui/views/sessions.test.ts --run` — passed 2 test files / 109 tests.
- `pnpm exec vitest --config test/vitest/vitest.plugins.config.ts src/plugins/runtime/runtime-model-auth.runtime.test.ts --run` — passed 1 test file / 5 tests.
- `pnpm run plugin-sdk:api:check` — passed.
- `pnpm run config:docs:check` — passed.
- `pnpm run plugin-sdk:surface:check` — passed with 0 package-exported forbidden subpaths.
- `git diff --check` — passed.

What regression coverage was added or updated?
The coverage now includes generated-title config opt-in, runtime model/auth forwarding, transcript filtering, input caps, manual title precedence, stale async write skip, post-reply metadata notification, reset/rollover cleanup, gateway row/search/event behavior, and Control UI event patch/filter/display behavior.

What failed before this fix, if known?
Before the current scope shrink, the PR had grown to include unrelated helper/API/test-routing changes. Earlier review also found that manual `label`/`origin.label` sessions could still reach transcript/title generation; that path is now covered by focused tests.

## Risk checklist

Did user-visible behavior change? (`Yes/No`)
Yes, but only when `sessionTitle.enabled` is true. Default behavior remains unchanged.

Did config, environment, or migration behavior change? (`Yes/No`)
Yes for config: a default-off `sessionTitle` section is added and documented. No migration/backfill is added.

Did security, auth, secrets, network, or tool execution behavior change? (`Yes/No`)
Yes for auth/model routing within the title worker: it uses the active session model/auth context. No new secrets, provider capabilities, network policy, or tool-execution surface is added.

What is the highest-risk area?
The highest-risk area is sending bounded transcript excerpts to the title model after the feature is enabled.

How is that risk mitigated?
The feature is default-off, skips manually titled sessions, filters heartbeat/inter-session/tool-mediated provenance, ignores textless/media-only records, caps input size, runs in the background, and does not block reply delivery.

What is the next action?
Run local submit gates, submit the single-commit scoped update, and let remote CI settle.

What is still waiting on author, maintainer, CI, or external proof?
Remote CI and maintainer review are still pending after submit. Product/privacy acceptance of the opt-in title behavior remains a maintainer decision.

## Current review state

Which bot or reviewer comments were addressed?

- RF-001 (`status: waiting on author` label): addressed by this single-commit scoped update and current verification; label state remains remote-maintainer/bot state until submit/settle.
- RF-002 (wait for exact-head required checks): pending remote CI after submit; the local exact diff has focused validation evidence.
- RF-003 (optional Control UI visual proof): not added. Focused UI controller/view tests cover event patch/filter/display behavior; live visual proof remains a limitation disclosed above.
- RF-004 (privacy, cost, disclosure boundary): disclosed as maintainer-owned risk. The implementation is opt-in/default-off, bounded, manual-title preserving, and non-blocking.
- RF-005 (config/session-state compatibility surface): addressed as an additive/default-off config and additive `autoTitle` session metadata; no migration/backfill is added.
- RF-006 (public provider-auth helper expansion): fixed/stale for this current diff. The public runtime-auth helper API expansion was removed; the remaining Plugin SDK API hash change is for public config/session type surface only.
- RF-007 (exact-head broad CI still in progress): pending remote CI after submit; not locally actionable before pushing the rewritten head.
- RF-008 (repair-lane/product/security/auth approval): disclosed as maintainer decision. This update keeps the PR scoped to the linked feature and does not expand provider/channel/plugin capabilities.
